lines.text: Marked, and you came to me. Smart. Nobody in the Sink cares what colour your name is. Now what's it worth?
One of Ninety-Nine's. You know what your people cost me? I'll tell you the number. Then I'll tell you what you're going to cost them.
Friend! Sit down, the car doesn't stop, that's the whole trick of it. What do you need and what's it worth to you?
Five points, warm Site Zero stack, candles. Nobody in your account signs for tending them. That's labour, friend. Labour has a bill.
Your schedule sends an unnamed load below the Sink. That's the trouble, friend: an address nobody admits is still a bill someone pays.
I still put that bill at Ninety-Nine's door. A note dated last month doesn't pay it. Keep the original, friend; this city likes to change its handwriting.
Three subscribers alive, friend. The notice calls it collection. That's the price I put on being polite. They can still argue about the account.
A Wake. Day what? Doesn't matter. In the Sink you were a person the moment you could pay.
Read the Chronicle, friend. What a choice costs is written there. What it means? That's the trouble.
Friend! Sit down, the car doesn't stop, that's the whole trick of it. What do you need and what's it worth to you?

barks.text: Forty minutes round. I've done it eleven thousand times. I know every face on every terrace. That's the trouble with knowing.
